entity.name: David Montero Crespo
entity.description: Creator and lead maintainer of Velxio, an open-source (AGPLv3) multi-board emulator and circuit simulator for Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Pico, STM32 and Raspberry Pi. Based in Uruguay and working on Velxio full-time.

projects.name: Velxio
projects.description: Velxio is an open-source multi-board emulator and circuit simulator that runs in the browser at velxio.dev or self-hosted with a single Docker command. Users write Arduino C++, MicroPython or ESP-IDF code, compile it and run it on real CPU emulation across 40 boards and 5 CPU families (AVR8, ARM Cortex-M RP2040/RP2350/STM32, Xtensa ESP32/ESP32-S3, RISC-V ESP32-C3/C6 and ARM Cortex-A Raspberry Pi), wired to 150+ interactive components: displays, sensors, motors, logic ICs and analog parts, with a SPICE electrical layer, an oscilloscope, emulated WiFi and custom chips compiled to WebAssembly. It ships more than 400 ready-to-run examples and is used by students, teachers, universities and makers to learn and prototype embedded systems without hardware. Since its release in March 2026 the repository has gathered 3,600+ stars and 390+ forks, and hardware partners Espressif, DFRobot, M5Stack, Seeed Studio and Pimoroni have supported it. Velxio is sustained with an open-core model: the hosted velxio.dev adds paid features on top of the open-source core, the main one being an AI agent that creates circuits from a plain-language request (it picks the board and parts, wires them, writes and compiles the code and runs the simulation to debug it). FLOSS/fund support would pay for full-time work on the open-source core: new boards and peripherals, emulation accuracy, the self-hosted image, documentation and community support.
